Rashi on Pesachim 80a:10:1.hebrew: מחגיגתו - של מחר, שאתה מטמאו כל שבעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:10:1.english: From his Festival peace-offering - Of tomorrow, for you render him impure [for] all seven [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:11:1.hebrew: אפשר דעביד - חגיגתו בשביעי של פסח, שהוא שמיני שלו, דהא כל ז' תשלומין אית ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:11:1.english: It is possible that he will perform - his Festival peace-offering on the seventh [day] of Passover, which is his eighth [day], for all seven [days] have compensation [for it].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:13:1.hebrew: קסבר כולן - הימים של רגל תשלומין של ראשון הן, ואינן תשלומין זה לזה. ופלוגתא היא בחגיגה (דף ט:), ומאן דאית ליה כולן תשלומין לראשון, סבר היכא דלא חזי לראשון תו לא חזי:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:13:1.english: He holds [that] all of them - the days of the Festival are redress for the first [day], and they are not redress for one another. And this is a dispute in Chagigah (9b), and the one who holds [that] all of them are redress for the first [day] holds [that] where one is not fit for the first [day], he is no longer fit.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:14:1.english: Who will listen to you - To be sent on a distant journey.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:14:2.hebrew: וכי עקר משכניה וסיכיה - אהלו ויתדותיו; ורהיט בתמיה: מי ישמע לנו להטריח עצמו? הילכך, הא עדיפא כרב:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:14:2.english: And would he uproot his tent and his pegs - [Meaning] his tent and his pegs; "and run" [is said] as a rhetorical question: who will listen to us to trouble himself? Therefore, this [approach] is preferable, in accordance with Rav.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:15:1.english: The majority of them [were] zavim - For they cannot perform [the Paschal offering] on the first [Pesaḥ].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:19:1.english: There is no redress for a Paschal lamb that is brought in impurity - And the zavim do not observe the second [Pesach], even if they became pure.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:1:1.hebrew: לא תוכל לזבוח את הפסח באחד - בשביל יחיד לא תזבחנו, שיהא אותו היחיד גורם ומועיל בשחיטתו שום צד נטיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:1:1.english: You may not sacrifice the Paschal lamb in any one - On account of a single individual you shall not slaughter it, so that that individual would cause or contribute any tipping [of the balance] in its slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:20:1.hebrew: רב הונא סבר טומאה דחויה היא בציבור - ובקושי הותר להקריבו, הלכך לא משוינן להו בטהורים למידחי טמאין לשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:20:1.english: Rav Huna holds that ritual impurity is overridden for the community - and it was only with difficulty that it was permitted to offer it; therefore, we do not treat them as pure [individuals] to defer the impure [individuals] to the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:21:1.hebrew: ורב אדא סבר היתר הוא בציבור - ומשוינן להו בטהורין, ודחו זבין לשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:21:1.english: And Rav Adda holds it is permitted for the public - And we treat them as pure, and zavim are deferred to the second [Pesaḥ].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:2:1.hebrew: איקרי קהל - ומילתא מפ' בהוריות (דף ה:), דקאמר ליה רחמנא ליעקב "גוי וקהל גוים יהיה ממך", וכבר נולדו לו כל השבטים חוץ מבנימין. הילכך, שבט אחד חשוב כציבור ולא מידחי לשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:2:1.english: Is called a community - And the matter is explained in Horayot (5b), as the Merciful One said to Jacob: "A nation and a community of nations shall be from you" [Genesis 35:11], and all the [other] tribes had already been born to him except for Benjamin. Therefore, one tribe is considered like a congregation and is not deferred to the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:3:1.english: They shall perform [it] in impurity - Even [the] pure [ones], if they wish.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:4:1.english: They render one of them impure - So that the majority will be impure, and all of them will perform [the Paschal offering] in impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:5:1.english: That the ritually impure outnumbered the ritually pure by one - For the ritually pure are not fit [to offer] on the first [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:6:1.hebrew: הדר' קושיין לדוכתיה - דהוו להו פלגא ופלגא, והללו יעשו לעצמן והללו יעשו לעצמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:6:1.english: Our question has returned to its place - For they are half and half, and these should perform [it] on their own and those should perform [it] on their own.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:7:1.hebrew: אלא ה"ק כו' - ולעולם מחצה על מחצה דווקא קתני, וה"ק רב: אי משכחת תנא דאית ליה כת"ק, דאמר פלגא ופלגא לא עבדי טהורין בטומאה כדקתני הללו עושין לעצמן, וכרבי יהודה, דאמר אין קרבן ציבור חלוק — מכי עביד קהל בטומאה בראשון, לא מפליג למיעבד טהורין בטהרה, דאוסר ליחלק, שגנאי הדבר, דמוכחא מילתא בהדיא כשנזהרין אלו מאלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:7:1.english: Rather, this is what [he] says, etc. - And indeed, [it] teaches "half and half" specifically, and this is what Rav says: If you find a tanna who holds in accordance with the first tanna, who says [that when it is] half and half, the pure ones do not perform [it] in impurity, as it teaches, "these perform [it] for themselves," and [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says [that] a communal offering is not divided — once the congregation performs [it] in impurity on the first [Pesach], he does not divide [them] so that the pure ones perform [it] in purity, for he forbids [it] to be divided, as the matter is unseemly, since it is clearly evident when these keep away from those.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:7:2.english: They render one of them impure with a creeping animal - And [thus] they will all perform it in [a state of] impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 80a:9:1.hebrew: שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ - הואיל וחזי לאורתא, הילכך אין מכריע את הציבור לטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80a:9:1.english: One may slaughter and sprinkle [the blood] for someone impure from a creeping animal - Since he is fit [to eat the offering] in the evening, therefore he does not tip [the balance of] the community toward impurity.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:10:1.hebrew: אתה מדחהו מחגיגתו - ואם תאמר: והא קיימא לן בתמיד נשחט (לעיל פסחים סב.) ערל וטמא משלחים קרבנותיהן? ותירץ ריב"א: הואיל והיא חובה לבא ברגל, יש לה דין עולת ראייה, דדרשינן בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ד:) דטמא פטור מן הראייה, שנאמר: "ובאת שמה והבאתם שמה" כו'; וכן איתא בירושלמי, דאיתקש לעולת ראייה. ואם תאמר: השתא, כשמשלחהו בדרך רחוקה, נמי מדחהו מחגיגתו, שאינו יכול לבא ביום טוב מחוץ לתחום, וכיון דלא חזי בראשון, לא חזי בשני? ויש לומר: דיכול לבא ולעשות ביום ראשון מה"ת, דתחומין דרבנן. ועוד: נהי דכשישלחהו בדרך רחוקה עד שעת שחיטה, שלא יכול לחזור לירושלים מבעוד יום, מכל מקום יכול לבא תוך התחום ויכנס למחר. ועוד: טמא וחיגר, דלא חזי בגופו בראשון, לא חזי בשני; אבל הכא מיחזא חזי, אלא שאינו יכול לבוא. וכי הוי יום ראשון בשבת, אף על גב דלא חזי, אמרינן באלו דברים (לעיל פסחים דף ע:) דעביד באינך יומי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:10:1.english: You defer him from his Festival peace-offering - And if you will say: Behold, we hold in [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (above, Pesachim 62a) [that] an uncircumcised person and an impure person send their offerings [via an agent]? And Riba answered: Since it is an obligation to come on the festival, it has the law of a burnt offering of appearance [olat re'iyah], as we expound in the first chapter of Chagigah (4b) that an impure person is exempt from the appearance [offering], as it is stated: "And you shall come there, and you shall bring there," etc.; and so it is in the Yerushalmi, that it is compared to the burnt offering of appearance. And if you will say: Now, when one sends him on a distant road, you also defer him from his Festival peace-offering, because he cannot come on Yom Tov from outside the [Sabbath] boundary [techum], and since he is not fit on the first [day], he is not fit on the second [day]? And one can say: That he can come and perform [it] on the first day by Torah law, for [the laws of] boundaries [techumin] are rabbinic. And furthermore: Granted that when one sends him on a distant road until the time of slaughter, so that he cannot return to Jerusalem while it is still day, nevertheless he can come within the boundary and enter the next day. And furthermore: An impure person or a lame person, who is not fit in his body on the first [day], is not fit on the second [day]; but here, he is indeed fit [in his body], except that he cannot come. And [similarly,] when the first day [of the festival] falls on Shabbat, even though he is not fit [to offer it on Shabbat], we say in [the chapter] Eilu Devarim (above, Pesachim 70b) that he performs [it] on the other days:

Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:14:1.hebrew: עקר משכניה וסיכיה ורהיט - הך פירכא ליתא למאן דחשיב דרך רחוקה מאיסקופת עזרה ולחוץ. ואם תאמר: ומה תקנה רוצה רב נחמן שיעשו, דהא רב נחמן גופיה קסבר בפרק מי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים צג.) שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ? ויש לומר: דקסבר דלאו תשלומין דראשון נינהו, ויכול לטמאותו במת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:14:1.english: Uproots his tent and his pegs and runs - This objection does not apply according to the one who considers a "distant road" [to begin] from the threshold of the Temple Courtyard and outward. And if you say: What remedy does Rav Naḥman want them to do, for Rav Naḥman himself holds in the chapter Mi Shehayah Tamei (later, Pesachim 93a) that we slaughter and sprinkle [the blood] on behalf of one who is impure through a creeping creature? And one can say: He holds that [the subsequent days of the Festival] are not redress for the first [day], and [alternatively] one can render him impure with a corpse.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:22:1.hebrew: לימא בהא קמיפלגי מר סבר טומאה דחויה ומר סבר טומאה הותרה - השתא לכולי עלמא טהרה מידחיא ולא טומאה, ד"איש כי יהיה טמא" משמע דהאיש לבדו טמא והציבור טהורים, ומאן דסבר טומאה הותרה — מיקרו שפיר טהורים. ומסיק דלכולי עלמא דחויה: מר סבר טהרה מידחיא, כדפרישית; ומר סבר טומאה נמי מידחיא, וקרא משמע הכי: איש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחים, אלא עבדי בין בטהרה בין בטומאה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:22:1.english: "Let us say that they disagree about this: one Master holds [that] ritual impurity is overridden, and one Master holds [that] ritual impurity is permitted" - Now, according to everyone, purity is deferred, and not impurity, for "If a man is impure" [Numbers 9:10] implies that the man alone is impure while the community is pure; and [according to] the one who holds [that] ritual impurity is permitted, they are properly called "pure." And [the Gemara] concludes that according to everyone, [ritual impurity is] overridden: one Master holds [that] purity is deferred, as I have explained; and one Master holds [that] impurity too is deferred, and the verse implies this: an individual is deferred, whereas the community is not deferred — rather, they perform [the offering] whether in purity or in impurity.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:8:1.hebrew: משלחין אחד מהן לדרך רחוקה - פירוש: אחד מן הטהורים, מדפריך: "ויטמאנו בשרץ". וקשה לריב"א: אדרבה, ישלחו אחד מן הטמאים לדרך רחוקה, דהשתא הוו טהורין רובא ועבדי בטהרה, דבכולה שמעתין אמרינן דמהדרי' אטהרה! ותירץ: דעולא גופיה אמר לקמן במי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צג:): "דרך רחוקה לטהור ואין דרך רחוקה לטמא", ולא היה מועיל שילוח טמא, דלעולם היה מצטרף לאותם שבירושלים. ואין נראה לר"י, דטעמא ד"אין דרך רחוקה לטמא" לפי שכשהוא בירושלים נמי אינו יכול לעשות פסחו אלא ע"י שילוח, אבל הכא יש דרך רחוקה לטמא כיון דמחצה טמאין, ואם היה בירושלים היה יכול בעצמו לעשותו. אלא נראה לר"י דמהדרינן שיעשו כולם בראשון ולא ידחו הטמאין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80a:8:1.english: "They send one of them to a distant place" - This means one of the ritually pure ones, since [the Gemara] asks: "Let them render him impure with a creeping animal!" And it is difficult for Riva [Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Asher]: On the contrary, let them send one of the impure ones to a distant place, for now the pure ones will be the majority and they will offer [the Paschal lamb] in a state of purity, as throughout this entire passage we say that we strive for purity! And he answered: Because Ulla himself said later in [the chapter] Mi Shehayah Tamei (Pesachim 93b): "[The status of] a distant place applies to a pure person, and [the status of] a distant place does not apply to an impure person," so sending an impure person would not help, for he would still be counted together with those who are in Jerusalem. But this does not seem right to the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak], for the reason that [the status of] a distant place does not apply to an impure person is because even when he is in Jerusalem he cannot offer his Paschal lamb except through sending [a messenger]; whereas here, [the status of] a distant place does apply to an impure person, since half are impure, and if he were in Jerusalem he would be able to offer it himself. Rather, it seems to the Ri that we strive for all of them to offer [the Paschal lamb] on the first [Pesach], so that the impure ones will not be pushed off [to Pesach Sheni].
